note: Second recording pass for lines whose first v2 takes measure rushed or very quiet (no listening possible here): each block keeps the neighbouring lines as spoken context and only its target line is ever selected. Words are unchanged; only beats (ellipses) and delivery tags differ.

blocks.why: all y14 takes 262-271 wpm (v1 s41 was 272): the hedges 'suitable' and 'might' need room
blocks.context_before: [curious] What might this be good for? Picture a delivery robot nearing a blind warehouse corner.
blocks.tts: With a suitable wall at the junction… a sensor like this… might give it an early hint of movement… out of sight.
blocks.context_after: Just a fuzzy blob: enough to say slow down, not enough to say who's there.

blocks.why: y06 takes 251-275 wpm on a five-word discovery line
blocks.context_before: That's why the answer is a likely location, or a rough shape.
blocks.context_after: Moved through known positions, the sensor behind that faint bump rebuilt the rough outline of a hidden U.

blocks.context_before: Many of their tests had help: safety-vest style reflective material on the target, which sends far more light straight back.
blocks.tts: Our clip's files… don't say if the walker wore any.
blocks.context_after: But in a separate test, the authors report tracking a person in ordinary clothes, capturing thirty frames a second.

blocks.why: y16 takes 2-6 dB quieter than the median line and low in pitch (the [softly] of the line before carried over); the takeaway should be calm but clear
blocks.context_before: For now, it's a promising clue, not a safety system.
blocks.tts: [warmly] Being out of sight… isn't the same… as giving nothing away.
blocks.context_after: To really hide, he'd have to block the bounces too.

blocks.why: v1 take x08_t1 measures 262 wpm (the script flags it: 'measures fast, listen')
blocks.context_before: Measure the extra delay, and you know how far he is from that spot. Not which direction… Just how far.
blocks.tts: He could be anywhere on this arc… all the same distance from that spot.
blocks.context_after: Now listen at a second spot. Another delay, another arc. On this side of the wall, they cross in just… one place.

blocks.why: v1 take x13_t4 measures 250 wpm (the script flags it: 'measures fast, listen')
blocks.context_before: Then, in a study published in 2026, a team from MIT and Dartmouth tried the small time-of-flight sensors, often called /ˈlaɪdɑːr/, found in phones and gadgets.
blocks.tts: [lightly amused] Don't expect your phone to do this yet… phone makers often keep the raw data private.
blocks.context_after: [warmly] Their new idea: a model that keeps track of what moved… so many weak frames can be combined.
